items.title: Booking a Hostel
lines: Hello, Sunrise Hostel. How can I help?
Hi, I'd like to book a bed for three nights, from the twelfth of July.
Let me check. We have a bed in a six-person room, or a private room for two.
How much is the private room?
It's thirty-five dollars a night, including breakfast. The shared room is twelve.
I'll take the shared room. I'm travelling on a budget. Is there somewhere to leave my bags?
Yes, there are lockers, but you need to bring your own lock, or you can buy one here for three dollars.
Great. And how do I get to you from the bus station?
Take bus number eight and get off at the market. We're opposite the post office.

qs.q: How many nights does the caller want?
Why does the caller choose the shared room?
Where is the hostel?

items.title: A Radio Announcement
items.text: And now some local news. Because of the heavy rain this week, the outdoor music festival planned for Saturday in Central Park has been moved indoors. It will now take place at the City Sports Hall on Le Loi Street. The start time has also changed: doors will open at five, not four, and the first band will play at six. Tickets already bought are still valid, but there are fewer places inside, so the organisers are asking people without tickets not to come. Free buses will run from the park to the sports hall every fifteen minutes from half past four. Food stalls will be available in the car park, so please don't bring your own food or drink into the hall.

qs.q: Why has the festival moved?
w: Because the park is closed for building

qs.q: What time will the doors open?
What are people asked not to do?
qs.a: Bring their own food and drink into the hall

items.title: Weekend Plans
lines: Are you doing anything this weekend, Nam?
I was going to go hiking with my brother, but he's hurt his knee playing football.
Not really, but the doctor told him to rest for two weeks. So now I've got no plans.
Why don't you come to the cooking class with me on Saturday? It's Thai food this week.
Sounds fun, but I'm terrible at cooking. Last time I tried to make rice, I burned the pan.
That's exactly why you should come! The teacher is really patient, and we eat everything at the end.
Well, if there's free food, how can I say no? What time does it start?
Ten o'clock. I'll pick you up at half past nine.

qs.q: Why can't Nam go hiking?
qs.a: His brother has a knee injury

qs.q: What does Nam say about his cooking?
qs.a: He is very bad at it

qs.q: What finally makes Nam agree?
qs.a: They can eat the food at the end
w: His friend will cook for him

items.title: A Museum Guide
items.text: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the City History Museum. My name is Thu and I'll be your guide today. The tour takes about an hour. We'll start here on the ground floor, where you can see objects from the first villages in this area, more than two thousand years ago. Then we'll go up to the first floor to look at the old port, which made the city rich in the seventeenth century. Please don't use flash when you take photos, because the light can damage the old paintings. If you need the toilets, they're behind the gift shop. At the end of the tour, there's a short film in our cinema room, and after that you're welcome to visit the café on the top floor, which has a great view of the river.

qs.q: How long is the tour?
Why can't visitors use flash?
w: It is not allowed in the cinema

qs.q: What can visitors see from the café?

items.title: At the Doctor's
lines: So, what seems to be the problem?
I've had a headache for about four days, and I feel tired all the time.
Not really. I've been working late on a big project, and I usually go to bed after midnight.
And how much water do you drink during the day?
Hmm, not much. Mostly coffee, maybe four or five cups.

That could be part of the problem. Too much coffee and not enough water can cause headaches. I don't think you need medicine. Try to drink two litres of water a day, cut down to two coffees, and go to bed before eleven.
And if the headache doesn't go away?
Then come back next week and we'll do some tests.

qs.q: How long has the patient had a headache?
What does the doctor think may be causing the problem?
qs.a: Too much coffee and too little water

qs.q: What does the doctor give the patient?

items.title: A Student's Talk about Recycling
items.tvi: Bài nói của học sinh về tái chế
items.text: For my project, I wanted to find out how much rubbish my family produces in one week. Every day, I weighed our bin before we emptied it. The total was eleven kilos, which surprised everyone. More than half was food waste, mostly vegetable peel and rice. The rest was plastic packaging, paper and a few glass bottles. So, in the second week, we made some changes. We started putting food waste in a compost box in the garden, and my mum began taking her own bags and boxes to the market. We also stopped buying bottled water and bought a filter instead. At the end of the second week, our rubbish was down to four kilos. My dad says the compost has already made his tomatoes grow better, so now he's the biggest fan of the project.

qs.q: What was most of the family's rubbish?
What did the mother start doing?
qs.a: Taking her own bags and boxes to the market

qs.q: Why does the father like the project now?
w: The family saves money on water
He weighs the bin every day

items.title: Changing a Flight
lines: Good afternoon, Sky Air customer service.
Hello, I'm booked on the flight to Da Nang on Friday morning, but I need to change it to Saturday.
Can I have your booking number, please?
Thank you. There's a Saturday flight at eight fifteen and another at three in the afternoon.
The afternoon one, please. I have a meeting on Saturday morning.
No problem. There's a change fee of two hundred thousand dong, and the afternoon flight is also fifty thousand more expensive.
So two hundred and fifty thousand in total?
That's right. I can take payment by card now, and I'll send the new ticket by email.

qs.q: When does the caller want to fly now?
Why doesn't the caller choose the morning flight?
How much extra will the caller pay in total?

items.title: A New Library
items.text: The new city library will open to the public on Monday, the fifth of May. The building has four floors. On the ground floor there's a children's area with games and a storytelling corner, which is open every afternoon from three until six. The first and second floors have books, newspapers and around a hundred computers that anyone can use for free for up to two hours a day. The top floor is a quiet study area for students, and you'll need to book a seat online. Membership is free for everyone who lives in the city. Just bring an identity card and a recent bill with your address on it. On opening day, the first five hundred visitors will receive a free cloth bag.

qs.q: When is the storytelling corner open?
What must you do to use the top floor?
What do you need to become a member?
qs.a: An identity card and a bill showing your address
w: A photo and a membership fee

items.title: Choosing a Present
lines: It's Grandma's seventieth birthday next week. Have you got any ideas for a present?
What about a new phone? Hers is really old.
I thought about that, but she says she hates learning new technology. She only uses it to call us.
She has a whole garden full of flowers. I was thinking of something more personal.
How about a photo book? We could collect old family photos and put them together with short messages from everyone.
That's a lovely idea. She's always telling stories about when Dad was little.
I'll ask Uncle Hai for the old pictures. He's got boxes of them.
Perfect. Let's order it online by Wednesday so it arrives in time.

qs.q: Why don't they buy Grandma a phone?
w: She already has a new one

qs.q: What present do they choose?
Who will provide the old pictures?

items.title: A Cycling Tour
items.text: Hi everyone, I'm Long, and I'll be leading today's cycling tour through the countryside. We'll ride about twenty-five kilometres in total, but don't worry, the road is mostly flat and we'll stop every forty-five minutes. Our first stop is a village where people make rice paper by hand. You can try making some yourself. After that we'll cycle along the river to a family farm, where we'll have lunch. The lunch is included in your ticket, but drinks are not. Please wear your helmet at all times, even if it's hot. If you have any problems with your bike, ring your bell twice and my colleague Mai, who rides at the back, will stop to help you. We should be back here at about four o'clock.

qs.q: What can visitors do at the first stop?
What is NOT included in the ticket?
What should people do if their bike has a problem?

items.title: Changing a Dentist Appointment
lines: Hello, I have an appointment with Dr Lam on Thursday at ten, but I'm afraid I can't come. Something's come up at work.
That's no problem. Would you like another day this week?
Dr Lam isn't working on Friday, but Dr Mai has a space at four thirty.
Hmm, I'd prefer to stay with Dr Lam, actually. He knows my teeth. What about next Monday?
Monday at nine fifteen or eleven forty-five.
Nine fifteen is perfect. I can come before work.
Lovely. And just a reminder, please arrive ten minutes early to fill in a form, because it's been more than a year since your last visit.
Oh, has it really been that long? I'd better not cancel again, then.

qs.q: Why can't the man come on Thursday?
qs.a: He has a problem at work

qs.q: Why doesn't the man choose Friday?
qs.a: He wants to see the same dentist
w: He is busy on Friday afternoon

qs.q: What time is the new appointment?
How does the man feel when he hears about his last visit?
w: Pleased that his teeth are fine

items.title: A Talk about the School Garden
items.text: Good afternoon, everyone. I'd like to tell you about our new school garden, which opens next month behind the sports hall. The idea came from a group of Year Eight students who were worried about how much food the canteen throws away. They thought that if students grew vegetables themselves, they might waste less. The head teacher liked the idea, and a local supermarket gave us money for tools and seeds. We'll be growing lettuce, tomatoes, beans and herbs, and the vegetables will be used in the canteen. Each class will look after one bed for a term. Don't worry if you've never done any gardening before. Mrs Thuy, who teaches biology, will run a short training session every Wednesday at lunchtime. We also need volunteers to water the plants during the summer holidays, so if you live near the school, please put your name on the list outside the library. Thank you.

qs.q: Why did the students suggest a school garden?
qs.a: To reduce food waste in the canteen
w: To make money for the school

qs.q: Who paid for the tools and seeds?
What happens on Wednesdays?
qs.a: Training for students who want to learn gardening

qs.q: Why does the speaker mention students who live near the school?
qs.a: They are needed to water the garden in the holidays
w: They will get vegetables for free
They can use the library in summer

items.title: Planning a Weekend Trip
items.tvi: Lên kế hoạch đi chơi cuối tuần
lines: So, are we still going to the beach this weekend?
Well, I checked the weather. It's supposed to rain all day Saturday.
Sunday looks better, but the bus there takes nearly three hours. If we go on Sunday, we'll only have a few hours before we have to come back.
True. What if we went somewhere closer? My cousin says the national park is lovely at this time of year, and it's only an hour away.
We could hire bikes there, couldn't we?
Yes, and there's a waterfall you can swim in, so it's almost like the beach.
Almost. Fine, let's do that. But I'm not getting up at five again like last time.
Don't worry. The first bus is at eight.

qs.q: Why do they decide not to go to the beach?
qs.a: The weather and the long journey make it difficult
w: The bus tickets are too expensive

qs.q: Where does the idea of the national park come from?
What does the man mean when he says “Almost”?
qs.a: He is not completely convinced the park is as good as the beach
w: He thinks the waterfall is too cold

qs.q: What did the man dislike about their last trip?

items.title: A Voice Message from a Friend
items.text: Hi Nam, it's Kim. I'm calling about the birthday party for Huong on Saturday. There's been a change of plan. We were going to have it at the pizza restaurant, but they've just told me they're closed for repairs. So instead, we're going to have a picnic in Thong Nhat Park, near the lake. Can you still come at three? Oh, and could you bring some drinks? I've got the cake and the snacks, and Duc is bringing a speaker for music. Please don't tell Huong anything about the picnic. She thinks we're just going for a walk, and I'd love to see her face when she sees everyone. If you can't come, just send me a message tonight, because I need to know how many plates to buy. Talk soon, bye!

qs.q: Why has the plan changed?
What does Kim want Nam to bring?
Why does Kim ask Nam not to tell Huong about the picnic?
qs.a: She wants the party to be a surprise

qs.q: Why does Nam need to reply tonight if he cannot come?
qs.a: Kim needs to know how many people to prepare for
w: Kim wants to invite someone else
The tickets must be booked tonight

items.title: Choosing an Evening Class
lines: I'm thinking of doing an evening class. Have you done any?
I did a photography course last year. It was great. Why, what are you interested in?
I can't decide between cooking and Spanish. The cooking class is cheaper, but I've always wanted to learn a language.
Cooking is once a week for six weeks. Spanish is twice a week, and it goes on for three months.
Twice a week is a lot when you're working. Are you sure you'll have time?
That's my worry. But if I only do six weeks of cooking, I'll just learn a few recipes. With Spanish, I'll actually be able to talk to people when I go to Madrid next year.
Then I think you've already made up your mind.

qs.q: What course did the man do last year?
What is the man worried about if the woman chooses Spanish?
qs.a: She may not have enough time
w: The teacher is not very good

qs.q: Why does the woman prefer Spanish in the end?
qs.a: It will be useful for a future trip

qs.q: What does the man suggest when he says she has “already made up her mind”?
qs.a: She clearly wants to choose Spanish
w: She should not do any class

items.title: Returning a Jacket
lines: Good morning. Can I help you?
Yes, I bought this jacket here last week, but the zip broke the second time I wore it.
Oh, I'm sorry about that. Have you got the receipt?
Here it is. I'd like a new one in the same size, please. A medium.
Let me check. I'm afraid we've sold out of mediums in black. We've got one in dark green, or I can order a black one for you. It would take about five days.
Hmm. I need it for a trip on Friday. I'll take the green one.
No problem. And because of the trouble, here's a voucher for ten percent off your next purchase.

qs.q: What was wrong with the jacket?
Why does the customer choose the green jacket?

items.title: At the Swimming Pool
items.text: Good afternoon, swimmers, and welcome to Riverside Leisure Centre. Please note some changes to this week's timetable. On Wednesday, the main pool will close at four o'clock instead of eight, because of a schools' swimming competition. The small pool will stay open as usual. From Thursday, our new lifeguard course begins. It runs for six weeks, on Thursday evenings from seven to nine, and you must be at least sixteen to join. The course costs eighty pounds, but members pay half price. Please book at reception. Finally, a reminder that the lockers now take tokens, not coins. You can get a token from the machine next to the café. Thank you, and enjoy your swim.

qs.q: Why will the main pool close early on Wednesday?
How much do members pay for the lifeguard course?

qs.a: From a machine near the café

items.title: Asking the Way to the Hospital
lines: Excuse me, could you tell me how to get to the City Hospital? I'm visiting my aunt.
Sure. It's quite far to walk, about thirty minutes. You'd better take the number twelve bus.
Just over there, outside the bank. But the twelve only comes every twenty minutes, and I think one has just gone.
Oh no. Visiting hours finish at four.
In that case, take a taxi. There's usually a taxi rank at the end of this street, next to the cinema. It should cost about six dollars.
Thanks very much. You've been really helpful.

qs.q: Why is the woman going to the hospital?
Why doesn't she wait for the bus?
qs.a: The next bus will not come for a while

items.title: A Radio Advert for a Cooking Class
items.tvi: Quảng cáo lớp học nấu ăn
items.text: Have you always wanted to cook delicious Vietnamese food at home, but never known where to start? Then join Mai's Kitchen! Our evening classes are for complete beginners, and each one lasts two hours. In week one, you'll learn to make fresh spring rolls. In week two, you'll make a simple chicken soup. And in the last week, everyone cooks a full meal for their family or friends, who are invited to eat it with us. Classes are small, with no more than eight people, so you'll get plenty of help. All the ingredients are included in the price, but please bring a container to take home anything you don't finish. Book online before the end of this month and get a free recipe book!

qs.q: Who are the classes for?
qs.a: People who have never cooked before

qs.q: What happens in the last week?
qs.a: Students cook a meal for guests

qs.q: What should students bring?

items.title: Planning a Birthday Party
items.tvi: Lên kế hoạch tiệc sinh nhật
lines: Dad's sixtieth birthday is in three weeks. Shall we have a party at home?
Our flat is too small for everyone. What about that restaurant by the lake?
It's lovely, but it's expensive, and Dad doesn't like fancy places. He'd prefer something simple.
OK. How about a picnic in the park, then? We could each bring some food.
Good idea. But what if it rains?
There's a shelter with tables near the playground. I'll check if we need to book it.
Great. I'll make a list of people to invite. Let's keep it a surprise, though!

qs.a: It is too expensive and too fancy

items.title: A Lost Umbrella
lines: Hello, lost property office. How can I help?
Hi. I think I left my umbrella on the number five bus yesterday afternoon.
It's a large blue one with a wooden handle. There's a small yellow bird on the side.
Let me look. Yes, we have one like that. It was handed in by the driver last night.
That's great news! Can I collect it today?
Of course, but we close at four. And please bring something with your name on it, like a bank card.

items.title: A Message About the Meeting
lines: Hi Paul, it's Jenny. I'm calling about tomorrow's team meeting.
I'm afraid I can't come at ten as planned, because my train has been cancelled and the next one doesn't arrive until eleven.
Could we start at half past eleven instead? Then everyone has time to get a coffee first.
I've already spoken to Sara and she's happy with the change. I'll send you the report by email tonight, so you can read it before I arrive.
If you can't change the time, just let me know and I'll try to join by phone from the station.
Anyway, thanks a lot, and sorry for the trouble. See you tomorrow. Bye!

What does she suggest?

lines: Good afternoon. I'm looking for a bike to ride to work.

Hmm, that's a bit more than I wanted to spend. Have you got anything cheaper?
This red one is one hundred and twenty, but it only has six gears.
I think I'll go for the grey one. Does it come with a lock?
No, but I can give you ten percent off a lock if you buy it today.

items.title: Choosing a Phone Plan
lines: Hi, I'd like to change my phone plan. I always run out of data before the end of the month.
I see. How much data do you use at the moment?
Five gigabytes, but I need much more now because I watch a lot of videos on the bus.
Then I'd suggest our twenty-gigabyte plan. It costs twenty pounds a month, which is five pounds more than yours.
Only for one month, so you can cancel at any time.
That sounds fair. Can I start straight away?
Yes, as soon as you sign here. Your new plan will begin tomorrow.

items.title: A Talk about Sleep
lines: Good morning, everyone. Today I'd like to talk about sleep, because many students do not get enough of it.
Doctors say teenagers need about nine hours a night, but most of you sleep for only six or seven.
The main reason is the phone. The light from the screen tells your brain that it is still daytime, so it is harder to fall asleep.
My first tip is to stop using your phone one hour before bed. My second is to go to bed at the same time every night, even at the weekend.
Finally, avoid drinks with caffeine after lunch. Try these three things for two weeks, and I think you will feel much better.

qs.q: How much sleep do teenagers need?
Why is the phone a problem?
qs.a: Its light keeps the brain awake
w: It makes a lot of noise

qs.q: What is the speaker's last tip?
qs.a: Do not have caffeine late in the day

items.title: Booking a Table
lines: Good evening, Marco's Kitchen. How can I help you?
Hello. I'd like to book a table for six people on Saturday, please.
Around seven thirty, if possible. It's my father's birthday.
I'm sorry, we're full at that time. We could offer you a table at six thirty, or at nine.
Six thirty is a bit early, but nine is too late for the children. I'll take six thirty.
Wonderful. Could I have your name and phone number?
It's Silva, S-I-L-V-A, and my number is oh seven seven, four five two, nine nine one.
Thank you, Mr Silva. We'll put a birthday candle on the dessert for free.

qs.q: What is the occasion?
Why does the man not choose nine o'clock?
qs.a: It is too late for the children

qs.q: What will the restaurant do for free?

items.title: Moving to a New Flat
lines: So, how's the new flat, Tim?
It's lovely, but moving was exhausting. We carried everything up three floors because the lift was broken.
Oh dear! Is it bigger than your old place?
Slightly. We have two bedrooms now, so Ben finally has his own room. The kitchen is quite small, though.
They seem friendly. The woman next door brought us a cake on the first evening.
That's kind. Do you need any help with the painting?
Actually, yes. Could you come on Sunday? I'll buy lunch.

qs.q: Why was the move so tiring?
What is the problem with the new flat?
w: There is no bedroom for Ben

qs.q: What does Tim ask his friend to do?

items.title: Instructions for the Machine
lines: Welcome to the Green Valley Laundry. Here are some simple instructions for using the washing machines.
First, put your clothes inside and close the door firmly. Do not fill the machine more than three quarters full.
Next, choose a programme. Press the blue button for normal clothes, and the white one for delicate things like wool.
Then pay at the desk by the entrance. Each wash costs three pounds, and the machine starts when you press green.
The wash takes about forty minutes. Please remove your clothes quickly afterwards, as other customers are waiting.
If anything goes wrong, speak to the staff member in the red shirt.

qs.q: How full can the machine be?
Which button should you use for wool?
Where do you pay?
qs.a: At the desk near the door
